ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Why You Buy What You Buy

fullPassage:
Why You Buy What You Buy

Good afternoon, students. Today, I'd like to talk about a topic that concerns us all: Money! Do you think that you spend money wisely? The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think. This is because human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors. Let me illustrate my point through the following examples.

The Anchoring Effect

In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. During the presentation, he said, "We're going to price it under a thousand dollars," which most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying. At the end, he said, "I am thrilled to announce to you that the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499." The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly seemed affordable to everyone. He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.

Let's say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see is priced at $100. That's too expensive, as you don't want to spend more than $50. Soon after, you see a similar jacket from a different brand with a $70 price tag. You think it's affordable, even though the price is still beyond your budget. This is because the first piece of information acts as an anchor that influences your decisions later.

Here's another common example. Look at the two pairs of sneakers. They both are $50, but the way their price is presented is different. Naturally, people are more drawn to the second pair. This is because the original price serves as an anchor, making the discounted price appear more reasonable in comparison. It is common for stores to use this kind of price anchoring as a way to encourage purchases.

The Endowment Effect

Now let's move on to another interesting effect. In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal preference for the two items. About half of the group chose the chocolate bar, and the other half chose the coffee mug. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items. But that's not what happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in the first and second groups were willing to make the exchange. Why is this? This is because people value something more when they own it. This is the basic idea of the endowment effect. People are less likely to give up what they already have or trade it for something else.

Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if it's temporary. Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it.

A free-return policy is another example. Say that a company is offering free returns on a smartwatch within 30 days of purchase. It seems like a good deal, since you can get a refund even after using the item. But once you take this deal and establish ownership of the watch, it is unlikely that you will return it.

As we've seen, our spending can be influenced by factors that appeal to our emotions and mind. I hope this short lecture gave you a chance to reflect on your own spending and helped you understand the reasons behind irrational purchasing decisions.

questions.passage: Do you think that you spend money wisely? The truth is that most people are not as rational as they think. This is because human beings are easily influenced by ①<u>psychological</u> factors. Let me illustrate my point through the following examples. In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth ②<u>to buy</u>. At the end, he said the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499. The crowd went ③<u>wild</u>. The tablet suddenly seemed ④<u>affordable</u> to everyone.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ①심리적 요인에 영향을 받는다. 태블릿이 ②구매할 가치가 있는지. 청중이 ③열광했다. 태블릿이 ④감당 가능해 보였다.
det.analysis: ❌ ② to buy → buying: 'be worth -ing' 구문. worth 뒤에는 동명사. ✅ ① psychological: 형용사 정상. ✅ ③ wild: go wild(열광하다) 정상. ✅ ④ affordable: 형용사 보어 정상.
det.tip: be worth -ing: ~할 가치가 있다. worth + 동명사(buying). to부정사 불가.

questions.passage: He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot ①<u>cheaper</u> in comparison. Steve Jobs used something ②<u>called</u> the anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information ③<u>they</u> receive when making decisions. Let's say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see ④<u>are</u> priced at $100.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 비교해서 훨씬 ①저렴해 보이도록 했다. 닻 내림 효과라 ②불리는 것을 이용했다. ③그들이 받는 첫 번째 정보에 의존한다. 처음 보는 재킷 가격이 $100으로 ④매겨져 있다.
det.analysis: ❌ ④ are → is: 주어 'the first one'(단수) → is priced. ✅ ① cheaper: 비교급 정상. ✅ ② called: 과거분사(수동) 정상. ✅ ③ they: 주격 관계대명사절 내 주어 정상.
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: the first one(단수) → is. are는 복수 주어에 사용.

questions.passage: A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an ①<u>equal</u> preference for the two items. This ②<u>suggesting</u> that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items. But that's not what happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in the first and second groups were willing to make the exchange. This is because people value something more when they ③<u>own</u> it. People are less likely to give up ④<u>what</u> they already have.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 동일한 ①선호도를 보였다. 이것은 절반이 교환할 것이라고 ②시사했다. 소유할 때 더 ③가치 있게 여긴다. 이미 ④가지고 있는 것을 포기할 가능성이 낮다.
det.analysis: ❌ ② suggesting → suggested: 주절의 동사이므로 과거형 suggested가 필요. 분사(suggesting)는 주절 동사로 사용 불가. ✅ ① equal: 형용사 정상. ✅ ③ own: 동사 정상. ✅ ④ what: 선행사 포함 관계대명사 정상.
det.tip: 주절에는 동사(suggested)가 필요. -ing형(suggesting)은 분사이므로 주절 동사가 될 수 없다.

questions.passage: In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying. At the end, he said the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499. The crowd went wild. The tablet suddenly seemed ①<u>unaffordable</u> to everyone. He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot ②<u>cheaper</u> in comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his ③<u>advantage</u> here. It works because people tend to ④<u>rely</u> on the first piece of information they receive.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 태블릿이 모두에게 ①감당 못 하는(→감당 가능한) 가격으로 보였다. 훨씬 ②저렴해 보이도록 했다. 닻 내림 효과를 ③유리하게 이용했다. 첫 번째 정보에 ④의존하는 경향이 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① unaffordable(감당 못 하는): 원문은 affordable(감당 가능한). $499 발표에 열광했으므로 감당 가능하다는 의미. ❌ ②③④ 원문 그대로.
det.tip: affordable(감당 가능한) ↔ unaffordable(감당 못 하는)

questions.passage: Now let's move on to another interesting effect. In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could ①<u>exchange</u> their items. A third group showed an ②<u>equal</u> preference for the two items. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items. But only about 10 percent were willing to make the exchange. This is because people ③<u>value</u> something more when they own it. People are ④<u>more</u> likely to give up what they already have or trade it for something else.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 물건을 ①교환할 수 있다고 했다. ②동일한 선호도를 보였다. 소유할 때 더 ③가치 있게 여긴다. 이미 가진 것을 포기할 가능성이 ④더 높다(→더 낮다).
det.analysis: ❌ ④ more(더 높다): 원문은 less. 'less likely to give up' = 포기할 가능성이 낮다. more likely는 반대 의미. ✅ ① exchange(교환): 정상. ✅ ② equal(동일한): 정상. ✅ ③ value(가치 있게 여기다): 정상.
det.tip: less likely(가능성이 낮다) ↔ more likely(가능성이 높다)

questions.passage: Let's say you are shopping for a new jacket and the first one you see is priced at $100. That's too expensive, as you don't want to spend more than $50. Soon after, you see a similar jacket from a different brand with a $70 price tag. You think it's affordable, even though the price is still beyond your budget. This is because the first piece of information acts as an __________ that influences your decisions later.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: $100을 먼저 보면 $70이 적당하게 느껴진다. 첫 번째 정보가 닻으로 작용하여 이후 결정에 영향을 미친다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① anchor: '닻'. 닻 내림 효과의 핵심 용어. ❌ ② barrier(장벽): 부적절. ❌ ③ reward(보상): 무관. ❌ ④ warning(경고): 무관.
det.tip: anchor: 닻 — 첫 번째 정보가 기준점 역할을 한다

questions.passage: Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if it's temporary. Consequently, they are likely to __________ it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 무료 체험 후 소유감을 느끼면 더 가치 있게 여기고 계속 소유하기 위해 돈을 지불한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ value: '가치 있게 여기다'. 보유 효과의 핵심 — 소유하면 가치를 더 높게 평가. ❌ ① ignore(무시): 반대. ❌ ② criticize(비판): 무관. ❌ ④ abandon(버리다): 반대.
det.tip: value: 가치 있게 여기다. endowment effect = 보유 효과

questions.passage: In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. During the presentation, he said, "We're going to price it under a thousand dollars," which most people assumed meant $999. He went on to talk about the features of the tablet and continued to justify why the tablet was worth buying. At the end, he said, "I am thrilled to announce to you that the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499." The crowd went wild.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 마지막에 가격이 $999가 아닌 $499라고 발표했다. 청중은 열광했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ 'the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499'. ❌ ① $999가 아닌 $499. ❌ ② 열광함(went wild). ❌ ④ $999로 예상(assumed meant $999).
det.tip: not A but B: A가 아니라 B

questions.passage: In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal preference for the two items. About half of the group chose the chocolate bar, and the other half chose the coffee mug. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items. But that's not what happened. Only about 10 percent of the students in the first and second groups were willing to make the exchange.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 첫째·둘째 그룹에서 약 10%만 교환 의향이 있었다.
세 번째 그룹은 초콜릿 바를 더 선호했다.

det.korean: 첫 번째 그룹은 커피 머그잔, 두 번째는 초콜릿 바를 받았다. 약 10%만 교환할 의향이 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② 'Only about 10 percent were willing to make the exchange'. ❌ ① 서로 다른 물건. ❌ ③ 동일한 선호도(equal preference). ❌ ④ 10%만.
det.tip: only about 10 percent: 약 10%만

questions.passage: Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if it's temporary. Consequently, they are likely to value it more and are willing to pay to continue to own it. A free-return policy is another example. Say that a company is offering free returns on a smartwatch within 30 days of purchase. But once you take this deal and establish ownership of the watch, it is unlikely that you will return it.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 기업들은 보유 효과를 마케팅 전략으로 활용한다.
무료 반품 정책에서도 소유권을 확립하면 반품 가능성이 낮다.
스마트워치의 무료 반품 기한은 구매 후 30일 이내이다.
무료 체험 후 대부분의 고객이 서비스를 해지한다.

det.korean: 무료 체험 후 소유감을 느끼면 더 가치 있게 여기고 돈을 지불한다. 소유권을 확립하면 반품하지 않을 가능성이 높다.
det.analysis: ❌ ④ 불일치: 'willing to pay to continue to own it' — 대부분 계속 소유하려 함, 해지가 아님. ✅ ①②③ 원문 일치.
det.tip: willing to pay to continue: 계속 소유하기 위해 기꺼이 지불 ≠ 해지

questions.passage: He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 설명하는 '닻 내림 효과(anchoring effect)'의 핵심 원리로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 사람들은 처음 받은 정보에 의존하여 판단을 내린다.
높은 가격의 제품이 항상 더 좋은 품질을 가진다.
할인된 가격은 원래 가격보다 항상 합리적이다.

det.korean: 처음 받은 정보에 의존하는 경향이 있기 때문에 닻 내림 효과가 작동한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① 'people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive'. ❌ ②③④ 닻 내림 효과의 원리가 아님.
det.tip: anchoring effect: 닻 내림 효과 — 첫 정보가 기준점(닻) 역할

questions.passage: This is because people value something more when they own it. This is the basic idea of the endowment effect. People are less likely to give up what they already have or trade it for something else. Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, '보유 효과(endowment effect)'를 가장 잘 설명한 것은?
ch: 새로운 물건을 소유할수록 행복감이 줄어드는 현상
소유한 것에 더 높은 가치를 부여하여 쉽게 포기하지 않는 현상
타인의 물건이 자신의 것보다 더 좋아 보이는 현상
비싼 물건을 구매할수록 만족도가 높아지는 현상

det.korean: 사람들은 소유할 때 더 가치 있게 여기고, 이미 가진 것을 포기하거나 교환할 가능성이 낮다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② 'value something more when they own it' + 'less likely to give up'. ❌ ①③④ 보유 효과의 정의와 다름.
det.tip: endowment effect(보유 효과): 소유한 것의 가치를 과대평가하는 심리적 현상

questions.passage: In 2010, Steve Jobs introduced the tablet computer to the world. During the presentation, he said, "We're going to price it under a thousand dollars." He went on to talk about the features of the tablet. At the end, he said, "I am thrilled to announce to you that the pricing starts not at $999 but at just $499." <u>The crowd went wild.</u>
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 'The crowd went wild'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: $999가 아닌 $499라는 가격에 청중이 열광했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ go wild = 열광하다, 흥분하다. 예상보다 절반 가격에 환호. ❌ ①②④ go wild의 의미와 다름.
det.tip: go wild: 열광하다, 흥분하다 (= go crazy with excitement)

questions.passage: In an experiment, one group of students was given a coffee mug and a second group a chocolate bar. Both groups were told they could exchange their items. A third group wasn't given anything and was told to choose either a chocolate bar or a coffee mug. This group showed an equal preference for the two items. About half of the group chose the chocolate bar, and the other half chose the coffee mug. This suggested that roughly half of the first and second groups would trade <u>their</u> items.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 their가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the first essentially and second groups

det.korean: 세 번째 그룹의 결과는 첫째·둘째 그룹의 절반이 그들의 물건을 교환할 것임을 시사했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② the first and second groups: 'roughly half of the first and second groups would trade their items'에서 their = 첫째·둘째 그룹의. ❌ ① 세 번째 그룹은 물건을 받지 않음. ❌ ③ 연구자 언급 없음. ❌ ④ 전체 그룹이 아님.
det.tip: 대명사의 지칭: their = the first and second groups'

questions.passage: This is the basic idea of the endowment effect. Companies often use the endowment effect as a marketing strategy. For example, many media streaming companies offer free trials to customers. Once customers use the free trial, they feel ownership of that service, even if it's temporary. Consequently, they are likely to value <u>it</u> more and are willing to pay to continue to own it.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 무료 체험을 사용하면 소유감을 느끼고, 그것을 더 가치 있게 여기며 계속 소유하기 위해 돈을 낸다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ the streaming service: 'that service'를 'it'으로 받음. 소유감의 대상은 서비스. ❌ ① 보유 효과는 현상이지 소유 대상 아님. ❌ ② 무료 체험 기간은 소유 대상 아님. ❌ ④ 전략은 소유 대상 아님.
det.tip: it = that service(그 서비스). value it more: 더 가치 있게 여기다

questions.passage: He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison. Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 닻 내림 효과의 작동 원리를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"사람들은 의사결정 시 첫 번째로 받는 정보에 __________ 경향이 있다."

※ 본문에서 영어 2단어로 쓸 것
accept: rely on
Rely on
rely on.
Rely On

det.korean: 사람들은 결정 시 처음 받은 정보에 의존하는 경향이 있다.
det.analysis: 'people tend to rely on the first piece of information'에서 rely on이 핵심.
det.tip: rely on: ~에 의존하다 (= depend on, count on)

questions.passage: As we've seen, our spending can be influenced by factors that appeal to our emotions and mind. I hope this short lecture gave you a chance to reflect on your own spending.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 화자가 청중에게 바라는 것을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"이 강의가 자신의 소비를 __________ 기회가 되었기를 바랍니다."

※ 본문에서 영어 2단어로 쓸 것
accept: reflect on
Reflect on
reflect on.
Reflect On

det.korean: 이 짧은 강의가 자신의 소비를 되돌아볼 기회가 되었기를.
det.analysis: 'gave you a chance to reflect on your own spending'에서 reflect on이 핵심.
det.tip: reflect on: ~을 되돌아보다, 성찰하다

questions.passage: He put the $999 price tag in people's minds at the beginning so that the $499 price would seem a lot cheaper in comparison. __________. It works because people tend to rely on the first piece of information they receive when making decisions.
questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오.

[Steve Jobs / used / something / called / the anchoring effect / to his advantage / here]

※ 대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능
questions.wa: Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here
accept: Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here
steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here
Steve Jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here.
steve jobs used something called the anchoring effect to his advantage here

det.korean: Steve Jobs는 여기서 닻 내림 효과라 불리는 것을 자신에게 유리하게 이용했다.
det.analysis: Steve Jobs(주어) + used(동사) + something called the anchoring effect(목적어 + 과거분사 수식) + to his advantage(유리하게) + here(여기서).
det.tip: something called X: X라 불리는 것. to one's advantage: 유리하게

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영어로 옮기시오.

"대부분의 사람들은 생각만큼 합리적이지 않다."

※ Most people로 시작할 것
questions.wa: Most people are not as rational as they think.
accept: Most people are not as rational as they think.
Most people are not as rational as they think
most people are not as rational as they think
most people are not as rational as they think.

det.korean: Most people are not as rational as they think.
det.analysis: Most people(대부분의 사람들은) + are not as rational as(~만큼 합리적이지 않다) + they think(그들이 생각하는 것).
det.tip: not as ~ as: ~만큼 …하지 않다 (동등비교 부정)

questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영어로 옮기시오.

"인간은 심리적 요인에 의해 쉽게 영향을 받는다."

※ Human beings로 시작할 것, 수동태 사용
questions.wa: Human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.
accept: Human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.
Human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors
human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors
human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.

det.korean: Human beings are easily influenced by psychological factors.
det.analysis: Human beings(인간은) + are easily influenced(쉽게 영향을 받는다) + by psychological factors(심리적 요인에 의해). 수동태 구문.
det.tip: be influenced by: ~에 의해 영향을 받다 (수동태). psychological factors: 심리적 요인
